title: Ambient unitaries don't enable shallow group designs
authors: Maxwell West, M. Cerezo, Martin Larocca
abstract: Characterising the efficiency with which designs over various subsets of the unitary group may be constructed is an important goal of quantum information theory. While it is now known that approximate unitary designs can be realised in depth logarithmic in the system size, it has recently been shown that ensembles of local nearest-neighbour sublinear-depth one-dimensional circuits over the matchgate, orthogonal, and symplectic groups cannot form approximate 2-designs over their parent groups; similarly, sublinear-depth ensembles of Cliffords cannot form a Clifford 4-design. In this note we show that this remarkable exponential separation is not merely an artefact of restricting to ensembles consisting of unitaries from the subgroups themselves, but rather that no ensemble of local nearest-neighbour sublinear-depth unitaries can realise approximate designs in the aforementioned cases, even when employing "ambient" unitaries from beyond the subgroup itself (possibly acting on ancilla qubits). This implies that various natural tomography and benchmarking schemes which involves sampling from these groups suffer from a dramatic circuit depth overhead compared to similar protocols which involve sampling from the full unitary group. We additionally conclude that, in all of the above cases, the known linear-depth design constructions are up to constant factors optimal.
summary: This paper proves that achieving approximate unitary designs over several important symmetry groups requires circuit depths that scale linearly with system size, even when utilizing unitaries from outside the defined subgroup. This result closes a loophole in prior work and has major implications for quantum information theory by setting fundamental depth overheads for benchmarking protocols.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental limits on how efficiently approximate unitary designs can be constructed when sampling from specific subgroups of the full unitary group, particularly when using local nearest-neighbor gates.
main_result: It proves that these limitations hold even if 'ambient' unitaries (from outside the subgroup) are used, implying that many natural quantum tomography and benchmarking schemes suffer from a dramatic circuit depth overhead compared to ideal protocols.
method: The analysis uses lower bounds derived from comparing the $k$-th moment channel fidelity ($\Phi^{(k)}$) against the Haar measure using invariant projectors associated with maximally entangled states.
model_or_system: The study focuses on various quantum groups, including the matchgate, orthogonal $	ext{O}(d)$, symplectic $	ext{SP}(d/2)$, and Clifford groups, applied to nearest-neighbor gates on a one-dimensional lattice.
key_observables: Approximate $k$-design fidelity ($\epsilon$), circuit depth ($L$), and the diamond distance between moment channels.
important_parameters: The required depth scales linearly with system size ($n$) for all tested groups, establishing an $\Omega(n)$ lower bound.
main_assumptions: The core contribution is extending previous results by showing that the limitation holds even when unitaries used are not strictly confined to the target subgroup (i.e., using ambient unitaries).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates how sublinear-depth designs over groups with invariant states are disallowed via lightcone arguments.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a general lower bound on design fidelity based on invariant projectors, specializes this for pure entangled states, and then applies these theorems to specific quantum groups (matchgate, orthogonal, symplectic, Clifford) to prove the necessary linear depth scaling.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous theoretical constraints on the resource overhead required for practical quantum characterization protocols (like tomography or benchmarking), directly impacting hardware feasibility assessments.
